long_biography.plain_text:
Providence Equity Partners was Jonathan Milton Nelson's answer to an investment idea his former firm declined. While at Narragansett Capital, he wanted to back a regional mobile-telephone company and became convinced that specialised investors could build media businesses with management teams. He left to establish Providence in 1989, concentrating on communications and media before extending the model into education, software and services.

Nelson's attachment to music preceded his investment career. He studied music alongside economics at Brown University and hosted a late-night jazz programme on commercial radio. Years later, he served on the Newport Festivals Foundation board. At Brown, he also endowed an interdisciplinary entrepreneurship centre designed to combine classroom study, mentoring and practical venture development.

Providence Equity Partners was Jonathan Milton Nelson's answer to an investment idea his former firm declined. While at Narragansett Capital, he wanted to back a regional mobile-telephone company and became convinced that specialised investors could build media businesses with management teams. He left to establish Providence in 1989, concentrating on communications and media before extending the model into education, software and services.

Nelson's attachment to music preceded his investment career. He studied music alongside economics at Brown University and hosted a late-night jazz programme on commercial radio. Years later, he served on the Newport Festivals Foundation board. At Brown, he also endowed an interdisciplinary entrepreneurship centre designed to combine classroom study, mentoring and practical venture development.
